title: Explicit univariate arithmetic circuit lower bounds
formal: Does there exist a family \(f=(f_d)_{d\ge2}\in\mathcal E\) whose arithmetic circuit complexity over \(\mathbb C\) is not \(O(\log d)\)? Precisely, \[\exists f\in\mathcal E\ \forall K\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall D\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}\ \exists d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge D:\ S_{\mathbb C}(f_d)>K\log_2 d.\] Every \(f_d\in\mathbb Z[x]\) has degree exactly \(d\); \(\mathcal E\) is the class with the uniform coefficient-bit algorithm and polynomial coefficient-length bound defined below. Circuits are unrestricted binary addition/multiplication circuits with arbitrary complex constants, and \(S_{\mathbb C}\) counts wires. This is a disclosed editorial specialization of Wigderson's Open Problem 12.1: it retains the not-\(O(\log d)\) threshold, selects the complex field permitted by the source, and makes explicitness precise using ITCS 2021 Definition 1.
why: This target asks whether efficiently accessible integer coefficients force unrestricted arithmetic computation beyond the elementary logarithmic degree bound, even with one variable and arbitrary complex constants. A solution would expose a source of circuit hardness that survives sharing and cancellation, providing a focused test of algebraic lower-bound techniques.
status_note: Wigderson's 2018 Open Problem 12.1 asks for an explicitly described univariate family of size not O(log d), without fixing algorithmic explicitness. This card adopts the disclosed integer-coefficient, deterministic coefficient-bit specialization based on ITCS 2021 Definition 1, with arbitrary complex circuit constants. A bounded primary-source review through 16 September 2026 checked the 2021 definition, its 2024 development and the July 2026 noncommutative and elusive-function results, and found no verified resolution. Status remains uncertain because no checked source explicitly certifies this same combined formulation as open; the search is not an exhaustive current-status audit.

importance.reason: A concrete explicit arithmetic lower-bound target that tests the strength of current algebraic complexity techniques.

sentences: The question asks for a family of one-variable integer polynomials whose smallest arithmetic circuits cannot all be bounded by a constant times the logarithm of their degree.
Each polynomial must have polynomially many bits per coefficient, with any requested coefficient bit and sign computable by one uniform algorithm in time polynomial in the logarithm of the degree.
The competing circuits may share intermediate computations and use arbitrary complex constants for free, while every wire into a binary addition or multiplication gate contributes to their size.
This explicitness requirement is a disclosed specialization of the original question, whose wording did not fix a coefficient-generation model.
A resolution would clarify how far efficiently specified coefficients can force arithmetic complexity beyond the elementary degree bound in a single variable.

definitions:
The index \(d\) ranges over all integers at least two. Write
\[f_d(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}a_{d,i}x^i,\qquad a_{d,i}\in\mathbb Z,\quad a_{d,d}\ne0.\]
Integer coefficients are embedded in \(\mathbb C\) in the usual way. All identities are exact formal polynomial identities in \(\mathbb C[x]\).

An arithmetic circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with one designated output. Input nodes are labeled by \(x\) or arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb C\). Every other node has two operand slots and is labeled \(+\) or \(\times\), computing the sum or product of its operand polynomials. The operands may coincide, in which case both wires are counted. Intermediate results may be reused arbitrarily often. Only nodes used by the output are retained. Size is the total number of wires, equivalently twice the number of binary arithmetic gates. Define \(S_{\mathbb C}(g)\) as the minimum size of such a circuit computing \(g\); every polynomial has a finite circuit, so this minimum exists.

Constant labels may depend on \(d\) and the circuit, with no restriction on magnitude, computability or binary length and no cost for constructing them. Their uses as operands contribute wires. There are no division, primitive power, comparison, branch, bit-extraction or coefficient-query gates. Negative constants permit subtraction to be expressed with the allowed operations. Depth, fan-out, intermediate degrees and intermediate coefficients are unrestricted; cancellation is permitted. Circuits are nonuniform: they may be chosen separately at each degree, without an algorithm constructing the sequence.

For \(a\in\mathbb Z\) and \(q\in\mathbb N\), define
\[\mathrm{query}(a,q)=\begin{cases}1,&q=0\text{ and }a<0,\\0,&q=0\text{ and }a\ge0,\\\lfloor |a|/2^{q-1}\rfloor\bmod2,&q\ge1.\end{cases}\]
Thus query zero is the sign bit, and queries \(1,2,\ldots\) give magnitude bits starting with the least significant bit. Zero has sign zero, and leading magnitude bits are zero.

The family belongs to \(\mathcal E\) if there exist fixed integers \(B,A,k\ge1\) and one deterministic finite-program Turing machine \(M\) such that, for all \(d\ge2\) and \(0\le i\le d\),
\[|a_{d,i}|<2^{d^B},\]
and, for every additional index \(0\le q\le d^B\), \(M\) on input \(\mathrm{bin}(d)\#\mathrm{bin}(i)\#\mathrm{bin}(q)\) outputs exactly \(\mathrm{query}(a_{d,i},q)\) within
\[A(1+\lceil\log_2 d\rceil)^k\]
steps. Binary representations have no leading zeroes, with zero represented by \(0\); \(\#\) is a separator. The coefficient bound permits at most \(d^B\) magnitude bits, and this query range includes them all and the sign. Every valid input therefore has length \(O_B(\log d)\). The same machine and constants work for every degree and query. They may depend on the family.

Here \(M\) is an ordinary deterministic multitape bit Turing machine: it has a fixed finite alphabet, a fixed finite number of work tapes initially blank and a read-only input tape; each transition reads and updates only the symbols under its heads and moves each head by at most one cell. Output is charged. No randomization, advice, oracle, unbounded-precision primitive or input-dependent precomputed table is supplied. No behavior is required outside the stated valid query domain. Any fixed standard Turing-machine convention yields the same class because arbitrary fixed polynomial time bounds are allowed.

The explicitness requirement gives access to individual coefficient bits; it does not require printing whole coefficients or the entire coefficient list in time polynomial in \(\log d\). This bit-computation algorithm is separate from the complex arithmetic circuits whose size is measured. The target says that \(S_{\mathbb C}(f_d)/\log_2 d\) is unbounded on every tail, not that it tends to infinity at all sufficiently large degrees.
answer_criterion: Give a complete, mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed existence statement or its full logical negation \[\forall f\in\mathcal E\ \exists K\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \exists D\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}\ \forall d\ge D:\ S_{\mathbb C}(f_d)\le K\log_2 d.\] A positive answer must specify one family, its coefficient-query machine and constants \(B,A,k\), prove exact degree \(d\), coefficient lengths, and query correctness and running time, and prove the lower-bound quantifiers against all allowed complex-constant circuits. A negative answer must cover every family in \(\mathcal E\); its \(K,D\) may depend on the family, and its small circuits may vary nonuniformly with \(d\). Showing that one proposed family has small circuits does not refute this existential target. Mere nonconstructive existence, a lower bound only for restricted constants, formulas, bounded depth, monotone or noncommutative circuits, or a weighted sum-of-squares bound alone is insufficient. The target retains not-\(O(\log d)\), without demanding a stronger superpolylogarithmic or almost-everywhere bound. An implication from an additional unproved complexity assumption is conditional progress rather than an unconditional resolution.

context_blocks.text: The original source contrasts the \(\Theta(\log d)\) complexity of \(x^d\), the \(O(d)\) upper bound for arbitrary degree-\(d\) polynomials and nonconstructive \(\Omega(\sqrt d)\) lower bounds before posing the explicit not-\(O(\log d)\) question.
The 2021 deterministic coefficient-bit definition makes a family efficiently specified while excluding descriptions whose coefficients require more than polynomially many bits in the degree.

The 2024 journal work connects strong weighted sum-of-squares lower bounds to broader algebraic complexity separations, but its support-sum measure and broader coefficient-bit explicitness differ from this wire-count target.
Raz's July 2026 revision proves new bounds for noncommutative circuits and certain noncommutative rings, which does not establish the present claim over the commutative complex field.

Narayanan's July 2026 preprint constructs vector-valued elusive curves and improves lower bounds at restricted depths, while identifying exponential curve degree as an obstruction to the desired general lower-bound consequence.

checked_sources: Source recovery: Wigderson 27 March 2018 draft, Open 12.1 p. 145, asks not O(log d), not a superpolylogarithmic bound. Section 12.2 p. 146 defines binary +/times DAGs, arbitrary field constants and wire-count size. Choosing C is explicitly disclosed; no equivalence of rational-constant and complex-constant complexity is presumed.

The book's word describe does not supply algorithmic explicitness. ITCS 2021 Definition 1 p. 23:2 does: deterministic poly(log d)-time access to coefficient bits and poly(d)-bit coefficients. Integer coefficients, signed magnitude and the exact valid query range make this an explicit editorial specialization, not an equivalent quotation of every reading of the book.

The published 2024 version instead uses #P/poly, in Section 2 p. 16. Do not silently substitute that broader convention. Do not assert that the listed Pochhammer-Wilkinson candidate has deterministic poly(log d)-time coefficient bits: the candidate discussion accompanies alternative explicitness notions and a separate proof of that stronger claim was not verified.

Coefficient audit: sign query zero returns 1 exactly for negative integers; q>=1 returns magnitude bit q-1. Valid q<=d^B covers all bits under |a|<2^(d^B). The coefficient bound is polynomial in degree, while the per-bit running time is polynomial in log degree. For d>=2 any fixed polynomial bound with constant factor can be absorbed by increasing B. The algorithm is uniform over all d,i,q and has no advice; the competing arithmetic circuit family is nonuniform.

Circuit audit: arbitrary complex labels may be noncomputable as bit strings and are free scalars; this intentionally retains the strong source model. Each binary gate has two charged operand wires, including repeated operands. No restriction on depth, sharing, intermediate degree, coefficient size or cancellations is imposed. Powers are computed by actual gates and divisions are excluded. The model computes formal polynomials rather than approximate values.

Quantifiers: not O(log d) means forall K>=1 forall D>=2 exists d>=D with size>K log_2 d, allowing oscillations. Full negation covers ALL admissible explicit families and gives family-dependent K,D and separately chosen circuits at each degree. No uniform procedure constructing those circuits is required. Positive witnesses specify a family for every d>=2, not just at selected degrees.

This is an existence question, so the numerical/function 1/100 acceptance convention does not apply. The positive criterion includes an actual coefficient machine and proof of its complexity. It does not require omega(log d) at every sufficiently large degree, superpolylogarithmic hardness, or a separation of VP and VNP; those would strengthen the chosen target.

Historical check: Strassen's primary publisher abstract (SIAM J. Comput. 3(2), June 1974, pp. 128–149, DOI 10.1137/0203010, https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/0203010) states specific hard univariate examples allowing arbitrary complex constants, including coefficients 2^(2^i). Such a degree-d example needs 2^d+1 bits for its largest coefficient, outside this class. The abstract and metadata were checked; full-PDF access returned HTTP 403, so its proof and numerical bound were not independently verified.

CKW 2011 anomaly: Corollary 4.3 visually prints an exponential-in-d lower bound for a displayed degree-d polynomial despite its own O(d) upper bound with arbitrary constants. This occurs in both inspected author PDFs. Do not repeat or silently repair that numerical assertion. Only the adjacent polynomial-bit-length clarification and Open Problem 1.4 are used. Final PDF p. 36 equals printed p. 32; the earlier draft has that text on PDF p. 35.

The 2024 SOS measure counts monomials across summands, not unrestricted arithmetic circuit wires. Its broader explicitness also matters. The bounded audit checked its definitions and stated implications, without claiming a new proof or transferring its target into this card. Published PDF has 54 pages; the shorter author draft numbers the explicitness paragraph p. 11 rather than p. 16.

Later check: Raz TR26-061 revision 1, 30 July 2026, pp. 1–3, concerns noncommutative polynomials and rings. Narayanan arXiv:2607.15848v1, 17 July 2026, pp. 1–3 and Theorem 1, concerns vector-valued monomial curves and restricted-depth bounds; its abstract identifies the exponential-degree obstruction. Neither supplies this scalar commutative lower bound. The theorem/model scopes were checked; the entire new proofs were not independently reproved.

Since the exact combined statement is an editorial specialization rather than a verbatim later conjecture, scientific status stays uncertain.
